title: Effects of on-site Gaussian disorder in the ferromagnetic Blume Capel model
authors: Kimberly J. Silverman, Daria Lhommedieu, Alykhan Rajan, Kathryn A. Cooper, Richard T. Scalettar, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla
abstract: We conduct a numerical study of a generalization of the Blume-Capel model in which the crystal field $D_i$, which controls the local vacancy density, is site dependent rather than uniform. We employ Markov Chain Monte Carlo to compute the shifted phase transition line $T_c$ as a function of the width $σ$ of a gaussian distribution $P(D_i) \sim \exp( -(D_i - \bar{D})^2/2 σ^2)$ at fixed $\bar{D}$. We characterize how the presence of this on-site Gaussian disorder reduces $T_c$ across the second order transition line, and discuss how our results suggest that $T_c$ remains finite even at large values of $σ$. We also determine the effects of disorder on the tricritical point of the conventional, uniform, Blume-Capel model, finding that it significantly suppresses the first-order phase transition, eliminating it entirely at large values of $σ$.
summary: This paper numerically studies the effect of site-dependent Gaussian disorder on the phase transitions of the Blume-Capel model. Using MCMC simulations, the authors demonstrate that disorder suppresses the first-order transition while only reducing the second-order critical temperature, suggesting the transition remains robustly finite even for large disorder strengths.
main_problem: The study investigates how introducing site-dependent Gaussian disorder in the crystal field modifies the phase transitions (second-order and first-order) of the ferromagnetic Blume-Capel model.
main_result: The disorder is shown to reduce the second-order transition temperature ($T_c$) but keeps it finite for large disorder, while it strongly suppresses and can entirely eliminate the first-order phase transition at large disorder strengths.
method: The research employs numerical simulations using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method on a 2D lattice, analyzing various thermodynamic observables and susceptibilities.
model_or_system: The system is the Blume-Capel model, generalized to include site-dependent crystal fields $D_i$ drawn from a Gaussian distribution $P(D_i)$. The Hamiltonian involves nearest-neighbor interactions and local field terms.
key_observables: Magnetization ($M$), density ($n$), specific heat ($C$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), compressibility ($\kappa$), and the Binder ratio ($U$).
important_parameters: Disorder width ($\sigma$), mean disorder ($ ar{D}$), lattice size ($L$), and temperature ($T/J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on MCMC simulations and self-averaging over multiple disorder realizations, avoiding mean-field approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of density, magnetization, specific heat, and susceptibility on temperature and disorder strength, showing the suppression of phase transitions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effects of disorder on the second-order transition line, then addresses the suppression of the first-order transition, concluding with finite-size scaling and comparison to the Local Density Approximation (LDA).
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed quantitative understanding of how quenched disorder fundamentally alters critical phenomena in lattice models, which has parallels in disordered quantum magnets and spin-glass physics.
